summary: The mechanism is sound and the master profile supports it: _pre_attention_kernel time rises roughly linearly with CTAs per SM. But the floor is about 1.5-2 us per launch even at 18 CTAs, so only verify_16/verify_32 (and a little of decode_32) can gain. The headline effect is about 0.5-1% geomean, inside the ±1.5% CI, so judge the run on the kernel's own profiled time per shape, not on the headline.
justification: Profile of the current best (bd64bf9f9e904f02, archive/paired-heads-launch-cleanup-ab-tune-batch-gate/…profile.txt) gives _pre_attention_kernel at 2.1/1.4 us decode_1 sliding/full (18 CTAs), 1.7/1.5 verify_1 (144), 1.8/2.0 decode_16 (288), 2.2/2.3 decode_32 (576), 2.8/2.8 verify_16 (2304) and 4.2/4.2 verify_32 (4608). Above roughly 4 CTAs per SM (132 SMs), time grows about 70-90 ns per extra 1-warp CTA per SM: (2.2->2.8->4.2 us at 4.4->17.5->35 CTA/SM). That fits per-CTA dispatch/issue cost, not bandwidth (under 1.2 MB, 0.25 us at 4.8 TB/s), so cutting the grid 9x to (tokens, Hkv) = 512 CTAs at verify_32 (about 3.9/SM) should bring verify_32 to about 1.8-2.2 us and verify_16 to about 1.7-2.0 us. Weakest link: the expected targets (~1.2-1.5 us) sit below the intercept the profile shows. Even 18 programs take 1.4-2.1 us, because each launch has a dependent chain: a cold-L2 DRAM load, the reduce, sin/cos when ROPE is on (sliding decode_1 2.1 us vs full 1.4 us), then the store. Regridding does not shorten that chain. So decode_16 (1.8 us) and decode_32 (2.2 us) will gain at most about 0.0-0.4 us, not the 4% claimed for sliding decode_32 (more like 1-1.5%). The verify_16 and verify_32 sliding claims (about 4-8% per shape) are plausible. Under the load weights (sliding x46, full x16, geomean over 6 loads), a 2.2 us saving at verify_32 is about 2.2% of that load, about 1 us at verify_16 is about 1.7%, and decode_32 is about 0.3%. Geomean about +0.6-0.8%, which cannot be resolved by one run. Triton kernel times reproduce within about 1% (LESSONS), so the _pre_attention_kernel row in top_kernels is the readable outcome. A secondary risk is batch-1 latency: 2 CTAs of 4 warps, each owning 8 q rows plus k plus v, instead of 18 1-warp CTAs. The chain depth is the same, but per-thread work is about 4x, plus the RoPE sin/cos on a [8,32] tile. Expect flat to +0.2 us there; it shows in the decode_1/verify_1 kernel row.
confounders: fused-preattention-triton: this is the kernel being regridded and the base of the comparison, not an independent confounder. Its result shows the launch was the lever; this change only changes its decomposition, so any delta in that kernel row comes from the regrid itself.

paired-heads-launch-cleanup (+ fa3-hdim128-head-pairing): on full layers at batch > 1 the query output is the zero-padded [tokens, Hq, 128] layout. Every query in group g shares half = g % 2, so a group program writes 8 rows to the same half and 8 zero halves; the write pattern per program changes, not the bytes. Full-layer pre-attention is only 0.7-1.6% of those shapes, so the interaction cannot move a full-layer row beyond drift. The implementation must keep every padded byte written (zero half included) on every call, or FA3 reads stale bytes from torch.empty.

paired-heads-launch-cleanup-ab-tune-batch-gate: batch-1 full layers use the unpaired layout, so the batch-1 shapes (the regression-risk ones) exercise the PAIRED=False store path. Both constexpr branches must be regridded and tested. No measurement confound: the gate is config-only and unchanged.
interference: No companion is warranted. The change is confined to one kernel whose own time is profiled per shape and reproduces within about 1%, so a gain or a loss can be attributed without a revert. No landed hypothesis changes that kernel's grid economics (pairing changes only which half of the q row is written). An ab-revert of pairing would only move about 1% of the full-layer rows. The one plausible split result is verify_16/32 faster but decode_1/verify_1 slower. That is already readable from the same run's per-shape kernel rows, and the fix is a shape gate (keep the per-head grid when tokens*(Hq+Hkv) is below about 4 CTAs per SM, i.e. tokens < ~32), which belongs in a follow-up hypothesis, not a pre-emptive companion. The spec's fallback, grid (tokens, Hkv, 2), is also a follow-up only if batch-1 rows lose. With 5 attention checks left and fa3-window-trimmed-page-table in the judge, spend one check, not two or three.
rules_flags: None substantive: same math, same rounding points (fp32 RMSNorm with eps 1e-5, interleaved RoPE from the cached inv_freq, FP8 E4M3 q/k/v), no host syncs, no caching derived from inputs, no change to which keys are attended.

Implementation check, not a rule break: the per-row reduction over a [G, D/2] tile (sum over axis 1 of xe^2 + xo^2) can reorder the fp32 sum against master. That is harmless for correctness, but do not claim bit-identity. Keep the cache_loc store address (loc*HKV + g)*D so page_size 64 tests and kv_scale 1/64 tests still pass, and load k_scale/v_scale once per program.
G = Hq/Hkv = 8 under both tp8 (16,2) and dp (128,16), so a [G, D/2] tl.arange tile is legal. Under dp the grid is (tokens, 16) and must still cover every group; the dp tests in TASK.md exercise this.
open_questions: Is the ~1.5-2 us intercept (18 CTAs taking 1.4-2.1 us) cold-L2 DRAM latency on the qkv/positions/cache_loc loads, or the RoPE sin/cos chain? If it is the latter, precomputing cos/sin is not allowed (it is derived from positions), but ordering the loads so pos/inv_freq are issued before the qkv tile could hide it. Worth a follow-up only if verify rows gain as predicted.

Should the new grid be gated on token count, with the per-head grid kept for decode_1/verify_1, if the batch-1 kernel rows regress by more than ~0.2 us? Decide from this run's per-shape _pre_attention_kernel rows.
num_warps=4 with a [8,32] tile is 2 elements per thread per half. Would num_warps=2 cut per-CTA overhead further at verify_32? That is a cheap later ab-tune if the main run gains.
